# OpenSocrates 1.2.1

OpenSocrates 1.2.1 adds a public development-adjudication snapshot and a
bilingual teacher-question overlay without changing the six hosts' real
delivery or evidence boundaries.

## Adjudication snapshot

- The repository now carries 51 EN/KO semantic-pair decisions and 49 resolved
  disagreement records with strict Draft 2020-12 schemas, aggregate counts,
  referential-integrity checks, and committed hashes.
- `make adjudication-check` validates the tracked snapshot from a clean clone
  and runs adversarial mutations. It never upgrades the snapshot beyond its
  `ai_assisted_provisional_development` evidence grade.
- The immutable public snapshot is anchored by a checker-pinned versioned lock
  covering its 11 manifest-listed artifacts plus the manifest itself. The lock
  is not regenerated by the finalizer and contains no maintainer-held evidence.
- Historical packets, raw screening results, and reviewer artifacts remain
  maintainer-held. Public validation reports that boundary directly; it does
  not skip or claim those private checks passed.
- The published adjudication snapshot is not confirmation-grade human gold,
  not held-out, and not answer-quality evidence.

## Teacher questions across six hosts

- Every one of the 48 methods now has three unique English and three unique
  Korean questions for the active agent to settle before acting. The canonical
  overlay is schema-validated and bound into generated package identity while
  authored method content revision `1` remains unchanged.
- Claude and Codex lead their bounded hidden trusted hook context with the
  questions. Guardrails take priority if the hook budget requires a fallback,
  and complete grounded procedure reads remain mandatory.
- Antigravity, Cursor, and Grok Build receive the questions through their
  existing skill/content paths; no new hook or selector claim is made.
- OpenCode's stable bridge injects one question-led compiled procedure and its
  native fallback reads that same procedure without a duplicate preamble.

## Packaging and privacy

- Deterministic generation now compares all six host packages. Release checks
  reject evaluation or adjudication paths in every host and Claude Chat ZIP;
  those source artifacts are also outside the npm package allowlist.
- The selector still fails open, writes only authored OpenSocrates material to
  temporary instruction artifacts, and records no prompts, transcripts,
  credentials, workspace content, hidden reasoning, or user identity.

## Upgrade notes

Update every managed host together with:

```bash
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.1 update --host all
```

The released native runtime boundary remains Apple-silicon macOS
(`darwin-arm64`). This release adds no new live-host receipt; consult each host
support document for its existing validation level and remaining limitations.
